clauses.current_legal_basis: The order's own held text (38 FR 2207) designates the Department of Justice as Central Authority and states no end. The bounded searches current-law:usc (through 2026-10-09), current-law:ecfr (as of 2026-10-14) and later-events:ofr_catalog each have 0 hits for the order, so no held later instrument amends, revokes or supersedes it. Checked through 2026-10-14.
clauses.reason: The sole operative sentence designates the Department of Justice as the Central Authority to receive Letters of Request from a judicial authority of another Contracting State and to transmit them to the competent authority. The text states no duration, date or condition that ends the designation, the order cites no authority statute that could lapse, and the three bounded searches found no later order, statute or regulation that revokes or supersedes it, so the designation is treated as operative on 2026-10-14. Limitation: no text of the Convention or of any withdrawal from it is held.

research_rationale:
Read the whole order (38 FR 2207, signed 1973-01-19; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11698.txt): a recital that the Convention on the Taking of Evidence Abroad in Civil or Commercial Matters was proclaimed on September 15, 1972 and came into force on October 7, 1972, and one operative sentence designating the Department of Justice as the Central Authority to receive Letters of Request coming from a judicial authority of another Contracting State and to transmit them to the authority competent to execute them. The order states no duration, date or condition that ends the designation. The three bounded searches were read against their coverage notes: current-law:usc (release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09) has 0 hits for this order; current-law:ecfr (eCFR as of 2026-10-14) has 0 hits; later-events:ofr_catalog has 0 hits, so the Office of the Federal Register disposition notes record no amendment, revocation or supersession. The only other held text that names the order is the 1989 codification snapshot (ofr-codification-1989), which prints a SOURCE line citing it for a Title 28 provision; as a 1989 snapshot it shows history, not current force, and is not relied on as a current basis. Limitations disclosed: the order cites no authority statute (only the President's authority as President), and the packet holds no text of the Convention or of any withdrawal from it, so continuation rests on the held original plus the bounded searches finding no later instrument.

The three bounded searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes) found no pending-matter residue or later instrument, so the state is none after bounded search.
